cases.name: ok-with-detail
cases.desc: A successful MONITOR_LIST: three envelope bytes and the empty declaration it returned. SPEC.md 9 -- detail is present because status is ok.

cases.name: ok-without-detail
cases.desc: A successful CAN_RESET. The opcode has no response detail, so an ok response is three bytes and that is not a truncated one.

cases.name: refused-is-three-bytes
cases.desc: CAN_SUBSCRIBE refused with bad_params. Exactly three bytes: a refusal never carries a detail, so a client reading further takes bytes from a request that failed.

cases.name: busy-is-not-a-refusal
cases.desc: busy says nothing about the request itself. SPEC.md 9 -- a client MUST retry rather than treat it as refused, and the envelope is the same three bytes as any other non-ok status.

cases.name: table-full
cases.desc: table_full on a subscription install. SPEC.md 9.2 -- the device is out of slots, which is a property of the device rather than of the request, and carries no detail.

cases.name: unknown-status
cases.desc: A status this build does not recognise. SPEC.md 11.4 -- it MUST decode as unknown and MUST NOT be substituted for a default; in particular it is neither ok nor a specific failure.

cases.name: unknown-opcode-detail-is-opaque
cases.desc: An ok response to an opcode this build does not implement, carrying four bytes of detail. SPEC.md 11.3 lets a minor version add opcodes with any payload, so the envelope decoder MUST carry the detail rather than reject it.

cases.name: detail-on-error
cases.desc: bad_params carrying two bytes of detail. MUST be rejected: detail is present if and only if status is ok, and a client that has already decided the request succeeded would read those bytes as a detail.

cases.name: short-payload
cases.desc: Two bytes: an opcode and a tag with no status. MUST be rejected rather than read as a status of whatever follows.
